Derive the pressure distribution by integrating the radial equilibrium equation dP/dr = ρ·r·ω² for a fluid in rigid rotation, yielding P(r) = P₀ + ½ρ·ω²·(r² − r₀²).
Use ω = 10,000 RPM converted to 1047.19 rad/s (ω = 10,000 × 2π / 60).
Keep ρ as a symbolic parameter in the general expression.
For the numerical evaluation and plot, use water at 20 °C with ρ = 1000 kg/m³.
Set the reference pressure P₀ = 0 Pa (gauge pressure) at the reference radius r₀.
Choose r₀ = 0 m (the axis of rotation) and evaluate over the radial range 0 ≤ r ≤ 0.10 m.
Express the final symbolic result as P(r) = ½ρ·ω²·r² when r₀ = 0.
Compute the numerical pressure at r = 0.10 m and at several intermediate radii to show the r² (quadratic) growth, not linear.
Plot P(r) versus r over the chosen range, clearly demonstrating the parabolic shape.
Do not use the hydrostatic formula P = ρ·g·h anywhere in the derivation or explanation.
State explicitly that the effective centrifugal acceleration a(r) = ω²·r is not constant, which is why the pressure depends on r² rather than on r linearly.
